purpose: Unsigned S23 proposal for the separate gate reviewer. Never loaded or a sign-off.
subject: framing

refused.labelPattern: \bstates[’']?\s*rights\b|\bWar of Northern Aggression\b|\bWar Between the States\b
refused.reason: no option names "states' rights" as the cause, or relitigates it: the seceded states' declarations, the Confederate constitution's slavery clauses and Stephens's Cornerstone speech name slavery (SENSITIVE-HISTORY 3.1, refused; [SW 6.1], [CS 4.1]; 0021)

baselineEvidence.placementAuthority: docs/design/SENSITIVE-HISTORY.md section 3; accepted by 0046 and amended by 0074
baselineEvidence.scope: Carried authority/source pointers, not a claim to have newly rechecked every older primary source.

windowBasis: [I] Candidate review envelope, not an incident trigger, publication date or proof of receipt. A named act still needs its own source/date. Inherited windows are byte-for-byte unchanged.

facets.recommendation: [I] The premise and founding-document framing continue; 1862 laws can illustrate slavery policy but cannot replace the founding sources.

agencyReasonNotes: [I] No class-required agency reason. Preserve named actors in reports; do not invent a derived mechanic or use absence of a reason as permission to target people.

triggerRules.policy: [I] Whole-word rules from triggerMatches; use the live proper-noun allowlist as well. A match requests review, never assigns a topic automatically. No gate:none approval is supplied.

topicRules: Do not substitute states-rights language or treat 1862 legislation as proof of every founder’s motive.

examples.allowedOnlyAsWordingExample: The text names slavery rather than obscuring it.
examples.rejectExample: The cause was simply states’ rights.

remaining: Existing founding-document quotations remain exactly as reviewed; any new excerpt needs its own primary source and attribution.
proposedRuling: [I] Carry the reviewed baseline envelope; add S7 limits as review notes. Reject changed premises, hindsight and unapproved new wording.
rejectedAlternatives: [I] Treating this draft or its schema check as placement/signature approval.
[I] Filling source gaps with inferred counts, motives, causal coefficients or implementation.
